quote: MELLE, a robust single-pass zero-shot TTS model that autoregressively predicts continuous mel-spectrogram frames based on previous tokens.
We present a continuous-valued token based language modeling approach for zero-shot text-to-speech synthesis, thereby eliminating the use of vector quantization.

To assess the naturalness, robustness, and speaker similarity of MELLE, we employ multiple subjective and objective metrics: WER... SIM... MOS... SMOS... CMOS...

To assess robustness and intelligibility, we perform ASR on synthesized speech using both a Conformer-Transducer model and HuBERT-Large ASR model. We calculate WER between the transcripts and the ground truth text.
We conducted subjective evaluations using a crowdsource human rating system to assess MOS, SMOS, and CMOS ...

We engaged native English speakers with experience in speech annotation and evaluation to participate as contributors in a crowd-sourced evaluation. ... We evaluated 40 samples from our test set, each utterance was assessed by at least 10 contributors.

We conducted subjective evaluations using a crowdsource human rating system to assess MOS, SMOS, and CMOS, which correspond to overall speech quality, speaker similarity, and naturalness of the synthesized speech, respectively.
guideline: Each test sample is rated on a scale from 1 to 5 for MOS and SMOS, and -3 to 3 for CMOS.
Three types of mean opinion scores (MOS) are assessed: MOS for speech quality, SMOS for speaker similarity, and CMOS for comparative naturalness, using rating scales described in the paper.

For MOS and SMOS evaluations, each test sample is rated on a scale from 1 to 5, in increments of 0.5 points. For the CMOS evaluation, the ground truth sample and the generated sample are presented in random order to the participants, who assign scores from -3 (much worse than the baseline) to 3 (much better than the baseline), with intervals of 1.
